finalJustifications: Because Cost Explorer allows you to view and filter expenses by service, account, region and tag over time, with trends, forecasts and savings recommendations.
Because Cost Explorer collects for each report generated, and this signature ensures the quality and retention of the cost data.
Because Cost Explorer collects the metrics of CPU and memory of the instances to compose the detailed invoice by account resource.
Because Cost Explorer is the only tool capable of creating and applying tags in resources, based on the analysis of expenditure per project.

optionReasons.saa-ini-274:option:0: The Cost Explorer analyze and view expenses — it does not send automatic alerts by email when exceeding the average.
optionReasons.saa-ini-274:option:1: Billing alarms from CloudWatch there are, but they only monitor spending ESTIMADO Total — no alerts by percentage of budget or expenditure PREVISTO as the Budgets.
optionReasons.saa-ini-274:option:2: Pricing Calculator is a pre-implantation estimate calculator — it does not monitor the actual cost of the account.

finalJustifications: Because AWS Budgets allows to create budgets with multiple (real or expected) threats and notify by email or SNS, can even fire automatic actions.
Because Budgets prevents new expenditure once the budget is reached, freezing the provision of account resources.
Because Budgets recalculates the invoice by applying progressive discounts as the expense approaches the configured ceiling.
Because Budgets is mandatory in all accounts AWS new, and the alerts of 80% are enabled by default since creation.

optionReasons.saa-ini-279:option:1: Closing the proceedings knocks down the service — 5% of CPU does not mean that the load does not exist, only that the instance is oversized.

finalJustifications: Because rightsizing adjusts the TAMANHO from the instance to the actual load (e.g. m5.xlarge → m5.large) using the recommendations of the Cost Explorer/Trusted Advisor — Short cost without affecting availability.
Because rightsizing moves the instances underused to Spot automatically, changing the availability guarantee for immediate discount.
Because rightsizing folds the CPU available at the same price when migrating the instances to the younger generation of the same family of types.
Because rightsizing requires reserved instances: the discount of the commitment is what makes the reduction of size financially viable to the team.

optionReasons.saa-ini-281:option:1: The Lambda does not keep container reserved by timeout time — the environment is released at the end of actual execution.
optionReasons.saa-ini-281:option:2: There is no minimum time charged equal to the timeout — the charge is for the duration REAL in milliseconds.
optionReasons.saa-ini-281:option:3: There is no percentage surcharge per minute of set timeout — timeout does not fit into the price formula.

finalJustifications: Because Lambda payable by GB-implementation second REAL (duration × memory) — timeout is only a safety ceiling against locked functions, not a charged value.
Because Lambda round the charge for the nearest multiple timeout, then 15 configured minutes inflame each invocation.
Because the timeout defines the price of the invocation and the duration defines the price of the memory — the two added components form the invoice.
Why reduce the timeout of 15 minutes to 1 minute reduces the billing in 15 times, in the direct proportion of the ceiling configured.

optionReasons.saa-ini-283:option:3: BODIES organise CONTAS; within a single account they do not separate costs per project — this requires allocation tags.

finalJustifications: Because Cost Allowance Tags, after enabled in Billing, allow filtering and grouping costs per project/team in Cost Explorer — the standard showback/loadback mechanism.
Because cost tags automatically apply a discount per volume to each team, reflected in the monthly billing report.
Because cost tags move the resources of each project to separate accounts, isolating the billing by cost center in the organization.
Because cost tags are mandatory in creating any resource, and Billing uses them to compose each team's bill..

optionReasons.saa-ini-284:option:0: The RDS costs MAIS per hour of computing that the EC2 equivalent — no special hardware that makes it cheaper per hour.
optionReasons.saa-ini-284:option:2: The RDS does not resize itself down when idle — stalled instance still generates cost (except Aurora Serverless, which is not the RDS classic).
optionReasons.saa-ini-284:option:3: Oracle Licenses/SQL Server are NOT free on RDS — are charged via licensed-included or BYOL.

finalJustifications: Because RDS builds up operational work — backups, patching, failover Multi-AZ, monitoring — reducing cost TOTAL (TCO) by eliminating hours of DBA/DevOps.
Because RDS runs in shared hardware cheaper than the EC2, passing the economy of scale on the monthly bill of the bank.
Because RDS zeros the cost of computing when the bank is idle, charging only storage in periods without query.
Because RDS includes the Oracle and the SQL Server at no cost, the largest component of a budget DBA.

optionReasons.saa-ini-285:option:0: There is no double charge: the transfer S3 → CloudFront It's GRATUITA — you only pay the exit from CloudFront, Which is cheaper.
optionReasons.saa-ini-285:option:2: The CloudFront is not free — charge by transfer and requests; what is free is the origin portion → CloudFront.
optionReasons.saa-ini-285:option:3: The CloudFront payable by USO (GB and requests) — no fixed monthly signature.

finalJustifications: Because the AWS does not charge the transfer S3 → CloudFront, and the exit CloudFront → internet is cheaper than S3 → internet — in addition to cache reduce requests to origin.
Because CloudFront completely eliminates the costs of data transfer from architecture, absorbing the output to the internet.
Because S3 credit to the owner of the ticket the traffic delivered via CloudFront, reversing the sense of data output collection.
Because CloudFront charge only for requests HTTPS processed — the transfer itself never appears on the service invoice.

optionReasons.saa-ini-286:option:2: A AWS no fixed subscription per service — the charge is for consumption (hour, second, GB, request).
optionReasons.saa-ini-286:option:3: Create Account AWS is free — no US membership rate$ 200.

finalJustifications: Because the model is pay-as-you-go: without a minimum membership rate or contract — you only pay what is consumed, and commitments (RI/Savings Plans) are optional.
Because the AWS charges a fixed monthly allowance per account and returns the difference as credit when the use is below the contractee.
Because the pay-as-you-go model requires the pre-payment of credits, consumed according to use until they need to recharge.
Because the AWS works under a contract of 12 months renewable automatically, and the pay-as-you-go defines only the form of plotting.
